title: 对亚洲母亲无所不能的刻板印象(6)
desc: 对亚洲母亲无所不能的刻板印象(6)

paragraphs.en: Then there is the matter of love.
paragraphs.zh: 接下来，还有爱的问题。

paragraphs.en: Something that can be lost, amid these narratives of grief, loss and domestic enmity, is that our mothers are capable of great courage and warmth.
paragraphs.zh: 在这些充斥悲伤、缺憾与家庭矛盾的叙事中，我们很容易忽略一件事：母亲们也能拥有巨大的勇气与温情。

paragraphs.en: If they are sometimes meddlesome and overbearing, they can also give us so much that it puts us to shame.
paragraphs.zh: 她们有时爱多管闲事、强势专断，却也给予我们很多，多到让我们自惭形秽。

paragraphs.en: (This is the tough thing, a friend said about her intense and often frustrating mother, she's like this because she cares.)
paragraphs.zh: （一位朋友谈起她那位情绪强烈、常常让人倍感挫败的母亲时说，这是件很无奈的事，她之所以这样，是因为在乎。）

paragraphs.en: My mother emigrated from China to New Zealand when I was born, in the hope of giving me a different life.
paragraphs.zh: 我出生的时候，母亲从中国移民到新西兰，希望能给我不一样的人生。

paragraphs.en: In our home of two, we enjoyed an intimacy that could be intense and difficult.
paragraphs.zh: 我们母女二人相依生活，彼此的亲密浓烈又艰难。

paragraphs.en: Other times it was joyful, the two of us gleefully conspiring together like sisters.
paragraphs.zh: 也有些时候，日子充满欢乐，我们俩像姐妹一样，开心地一起谋划趣事。

paragraphs.en: She was – and is – tenacious and strong-willed and a dreamer.
paragraphs.zh: 她过去——现在也依然——坚韧、意志坚定，心怀梦想。

paragraphs.en: Her dreaming often took the form of buoyant and unwavering confidence in me.
paragraphs.zh: 她的梦想常常化作对我坚定不移、昂扬饱满的信心。

paragraphs.en: Contrary to the stereotype of the ever-critical matriarch, my mother believed I was destined to be among the greatest ballerinas/mathematicians/etceteras that the world had ever seen.
paragraphs.zh: 和那种永远在挑错的大家长刻板印象相反，母亲坚信，我注定会成为世界上最顶尖的芭蕾舞演员、数学家，或是其他领域的杰出人物。

paragraphs.en: (Imagine my indignation when I grew older and was confronted by the fact I was bad at many things.)
paragraphs.zh: （长大后，我发现自己很多事情都做不好，想想当时的满心不甘，恍如昨日。）

paragraphs.en: She impressed on me the importance of being conscientious and responsible, so I was delighted to discover as a young child, while flicking through one of her undergraduate law textbooks (she worked at a law firm in China, but had to get a new degree to practise in New Zealand), a note she had scrawled in the margin: "BORING."
paragraphs.zh: 她反复叮嘱我，做人要认真尽责。小时候翻她的本科法律课本（她在中国律所工作，但要在新西兰执业，必须重新考取学位），我惊喜地看到页边她随手写下的批注：“无聊。”

paragraphs.en: The memory comes to mind now because it was the first time that it had occurred to me that my mother was also a person in her own right, with her private world and gleeful rebellions.
paragraphs.zh: 如今想起这件事，是因为那是我第一次意识到，母亲本身也是独立的个体，拥有属于自己的内心世界，也会有调皮反叛的小乐趣。

paragraphs.en: For the most part, she seemed invincible in the way parents can appear to young children.
paragraphs.zh: 在年幼的我眼中，父母往往是无所不能的，她大多时候也给我这样的感觉。

paragraphs.en: As I grew older, I occasionally saw her in moments of exhaustion, feeling sadness about being so far from what she knew.
paragraphs.zh: 随着我慢慢长大，偶尔会看见她疲惫的样子，因远离熟悉的故土而满心伤感。

paragraphs.en: We moved to Hong Kong when I was 12 to be closer to family, and from then I began to get a sense that there was a whole other life in my mother that I had no access to.
paragraphs.zh: 十二岁那年，我们搬到香港，离亲人更近一些。从那时候起，我慢慢发觉，母亲内心藏着一整个我无法触及的人生。

paragraphs.en: When I asked my mum if I could interview her about her life, she instantly agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 我问母亲，能不能采访她，听听她的人生故事，她立刻答应了。

paragraphs.en: I spoke to her over several video calls, with me in London and her in New Zealand; she spoke freely, often with heartbreaking sincerity.
paragraphs.zh: 我在伦敦，她在新西兰，我们进行了好几轮视频通话。她坦然诉说，话语常常带着令人心碎的真诚。

paragraphs.en: Some of the stories she shared were familiar, lines from anecdotes that I had heard many years ago, but placed in greater context.
paragraphs.zh: 她讲的一些故事我并不陌生，是多年前听过的轶事，只是这次，她把完整的背景一并道来。

paragraphs.en: And when I asked her about her own experience of motherhood itself, she told me things I'd never heard before.
paragraphs.zh: 当我问到她身为母亲的切身感受时，她说出了很多我从未听过的往事。

paragraphs.en: She grew up as the eldest daughter of four in a large family in a city near Wuhan.
paragraphs.zh: 她在武汉附近一座城市的大家庭长大，是四个孩子里的长女。

paragraphs.en: As the eldest daughter, she was constantly reminded that she had to be like a mother to her younger brother, the prized son.
paragraphs.zh: 作为长女，她总被提醒，要像母亲一样照顾弟弟——那个全家珍视的男孩。

paragraphs.en: "I grew up in a very depressed environment," my mum said. Moving to New Zealand wasn't easy for her.
paragraphs.zh: “我成长在一个非常压抑的环境里。”母亲说。搬到新西兰的日子并不好过。

paragraphs.en: She took on itinerant jobs, drew on fellow Chinese immigrants to help with childcare, and often felt overwhelmed at being alone in a new country.
paragraphs.zh: 她打各种零工，依靠其他华人移民帮忙照看孩子，孤身身处异国，常常觉得不堪重负。

paragraphs.en: And yet she stayed. "I wanted you to have a happy childhood," she told me. "I didn't want my bad feelings to extend to your life."
paragraphs.zh: 但她坚持留了下来。“我想让你拥有快乐的童年，”她对我说，“我不想让我的负面情绪延续到你的人生里。”

paragraphs.en: Of course, "bad feelings" have a habit of finding their way into the next generation.
paragraphs.zh: 当然，负面情绪总会想方设法传递给下一代。

paragraphs.en: When my mum shared her story with me, I had the surreal sense that I was putting together pieces of a puzzle that had been somewhere in my subconscious since I was very young, things caught in conversations that I probably wasn't supposed to overhear.
paragraphs.zh: 母亲和我讲述这些往事时，我有种不真实的感觉：我正在拼凑一幅拼图，碎片从小就藏在我的潜意识里，是那些我无意中偷听来的对话片段。

paragraphs.en: But unlike when I was a child, when I could not fully believe that the past was real and my mother was once a child herself, hearing this now I felt an immense sadness about what she had been through.
paragraphs.zh: 小时候，我无法真切理解那段历史的真实性，也很难想象母亲也曾是个孩子。如今听完这些故事，我深深为她经历的一切感到难过。

paragraphs.en: We often talk about "digesting" or "working through" emotions, as if they are things to be shuttled through the factory line of our bodies to be broken down and packaged anew.
paragraphs.zh: 我们常说要“消化”或者“处理”情绪，仿佛情绪是流水线里的物件，可以拆解、重新打包。

paragraphs.en: My mother's childhood, however, seems so vast and unfathomable that it is hard to absorb.
paragraphs.zh: 但母亲的童年，沉重浩瀚，难以参透，让人难以完全接纳。

paragraphs.en: But for the same reasons, I cannot get rid of it.
paragraphs.zh: 可也正因如此，我无法将它置之脑后。

paragraphs.en: When we spoke, I told her that I struggle with the gulf between my life and the one she had; that I feel the weight of the sacrifices she made for me, and I spend much of my life striving to be worthy of them.
paragraphs.zh: 通话时，我告诉她，我难以跨越我和她人生之间巨大的鸿沟；我能感受到她为我做出的牺牲带来的重量，一生都在努力，希望配得上这份付出。

paragraphs.en: That wasn't how she saw it.
paragraphs.zh: 但她并不是这么看待这件事的。

paragraphs.en: Whereas I found myself dwelling on the hardships she had faced as a young mother, she remembered it as an energising experience – she finally learned to drive, for one – that pushed her to be the best she could be.
paragraphs.zh: 我总是沉浸在她年轻时为人母所承受的艰辛，而她却记得那段时光充满动力：比如说，她终于学会了开车，那段经历推着她努力做到最好。

paragraphs.en: "To be clear," she said, "I don't think I've made any sacrifice for you. I never thought I did something called sacrifice.
paragraphs.zh: “说实话，”她说，“我并不觉得我为你做出了牺牲。我从来没有认为那叫牺牲。

paragraphs.en: I never thought it was a sacrifice. I think you deserve all the things I have done for you. I wish I could have done more."
paragraphs.zh: 我从来没有把这些当成牺牲。我认为我为你做的一切，都是你应得的。我只遗憾没能做得更多。”
